summary: Backend regression testing for the invoice pin_display removal + Location=Post Site Name fix. All 5 pytest cases passed against the live preview URL. Verified: (1) POST /api/dispatch/invoices/preview lines have location == post_site_name and pin_display is null. (2) POST /api/dispatch/invoices/preview/pdf returns a valid PDF whose extracted text contains all expected headers (Shift Date, Location, Work Order, Actual Hour, Rate, Total Amount) and contains NO '#<pin>', '# <pin>' or 'CODE # PIN' pattern (parsed via pdfplumber). (3) When override lines are sent with post_pin AND pin_display 'PTS # 123', the backend strips pin_display to null in the response. (4) GET /api/dispatch/schedules?limit=3 still returns post_pin_display (e.g. 'PTS # 123') - reports/schedules unaffected. (5) GET /api/dispatch/reports/by-officer regression 200 OK.
critical_code_review_comments: dispatch_invoices.py::_gather_lines still computes and stores the local `code`/`pin` variables even though pin_display is hard-coded to None — dead code that can be removed for clarity.

InvoiceLine model still exposes pin_display as an optional field; consider removing it from the model or documenting that it will always be forced to None server-side so API consumers don't rely on it.

dispatch_reports.py::build_invoice_pdf still contains the `# ` pin rendering logic branches conceptually removed by the fix — file was inspected and now only renders plain location text, which is correct.

rca of the issue: Not applicable — this iteration validated an already-applied fix. Prior bug: invoice line location was populated from post_site.location field and a bold VENDOR # PIN line was rendered above location in the PDF. Fix: (a) _gather_lines uses p.get('name') first; (b) pin_display forced to None in both auto and override_lines paths; (c) build_invoice_pdf Location column renders plain text. Tests confirm no 'CODE # PIN' pattern appears in the rendered PDF text and every response line satisfies location == post_site_name.
